setup: CREATE TABLE countries AS SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('US', 'Americas'), ('DE', 'Europe'), ('IN', 'Asia')) t(country, region)
input.pql: PREDICT COUNT(orders.*, 0, 30, days) > 0 FOR EACH users.user_id

view.name: view_metric_wildcards_nested_join
view.yaml:
version: 0.1
source: "`{catalog}`.`{schema}`.orders"
joins:
  - name: users
    source: "`{catalog}`.`{schema}`.users"
    on: source.user_id = users.user_id
    joins:
      - name: countries
        source: "`{catalog}`.`{schema}`.countries"
        on: users.country = countries.country
dimensions:
  - expr: source.* EXCEPT (price)
  - expr: users.* EXCEPT (age, user_id)
  - name: region
    expr: users.countries.region
measures:
  - name: revenue
    expr: SUM(source.price)

why: Wildcard dimensions (alias.* EXCEPT (...), DB/metric_view.py:967) expanded to the columns Databricks expands them to, a join nested in a join (countries under users, a snowflake schema) read as a link from users, and a measure reading a column no dimension names (price), which the reference adds to its table (RE/graph.py, measure inputs). The view is created in the test schema from the yaml, its sources named with the {catalog} and {schema} placeholders the capture writes (no private name), each part backtick-quoted since Databricks reads a catalog's hyphen only quoted; its joins' on keys are bare, as people write them, so PyYAML reads each as the key true (KO3-40), which the reference reads too (DB/metric_view.py:825-909, join_cfg.get(True))
